@@ -0,0 +1,201 @@
+//! Login-state probing for subscription CLI providers.
+//!
+//! Binary presence says "installed", not "usable": a user with `claude` on
+//! PATH but no login sails through setup and hits raw subprocess stderr
+//! mid-run. Descriptors may declare an `[auth_probe]` (a local status
+//! subcommand such as `claude auth status`); this module runs it with a
+//! timeout and classifies the result.
+//!
+//! Classification is deliberately fail-open: only an explicit logged-out
+//! marker (or a logged-in marker that is absent while a logged-out marker
+//! matches) yields `NotLoggedIn`. Anything ambiguous — unsupported
+//! subcommand on an older CLI, unexpected output shape, timeout — is
+//! `Unknown`, and callers treat `Unknown` exactly as they treated binary
+//! presence before this probe existed.
+
+use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
+use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
+
+use crate::registry::AuthProbe;
+
+const DEFAULT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: u64 = 10;
+const PROBE_POLL_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(50);
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum CliAuthStatus {
+    LoggedIn,
+    NotLoggedIn { detail: String },
+    Unknown { reason: String },
+}
+
+/// Run the descriptor's auth probe against `binary` and classify the output.
+/// Never errors: every failure mode collapses into `Unknown` so the caller
+/// can fall back to presence-only behavior.
+pub fn probe_cli_auth(binary: &str, probe: &AuthProbe) -> CliAuthStatus {
+    let timeout = Duration::from_secs(
+        probe
+            .timeout_seconds
+            .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS),
+    );
+    let mut command = Command::new(binary);
+    command
+        .args(&probe.args)
+        .stdin(Stdio::null())
+        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
+        .stderr(Stdio::piped());
+    let mut child = match command.spawn() {
+        Ok(child) => child,
+        Err(err) => {
+            return CliAuthStatus::Unknown {
+                reason: format!("could not run {binary}: {err}"),
+            };
+        }
+    };
+    let started = Instant::now();
+    loop {
+        match child.try_wait() {
+            Ok(Some(_)) => break,
+            Ok(None) => {
+                if started.elapsed() > timeout {
+                    let _ = child.kill();
+                    let _ = child.wait();
+                    return CliAuthStatus::Unknown {
+                        reason: format!(
+                            "auth probe timed out after {}s",
+                            timeout.as_secs()
+                        ),
+                    };
+                }
+                std::thread::sleep(PROBE_POLL_INTERVAL);
+            }
+            Err(err) => {
+                return CliAuthStatus::Unknown {
+                    reason: format!("auth probe failed: {err}"),
+                };
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    let output = match child.wait_with_output() {
+        Ok(output) => output,
+        Err(err) => {
+            return CliAuthStatus::Unknown {
+                reason: format!("auth probe failed: {err}"),
+            };
+        }
+    };
+    let combined = format!(
+        "{}{}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout),
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
+    );
+    classify_probe_output(probe, &combined)
+}
+
+fn classify_probe_output(probe: &AuthProbe, combined: &str) -> CliAuthStatus {
+    let condensed = condense(combined);
+    // Logged-out first: logged-out markers often embed the logged-in phrase
+    // ("Not logged in" contains "logged in").
+    if let Some(out_marker) = probe.logged_out_substring.as_deref()
+        && condensed.contains(&condense(out_marker))
+    {
+        return CliAuthStatus::NotLoggedIn {
+            detail: first_line(combined),
+        };
+    }
+    if let Some(in_marker) = probe.logged_in_substring.as_deref()
+        && condensed.contains(&condense(in_marker))
+    {
+        return CliAuthStatus::LoggedIn;
+    }
+    CliAuthStatus::Unknown {
+        reason: "auth probe output did not match a known login state".to_string(),
+    }
+}
+
+/// Strip all whitespace so marker matching survives JSON pretty-printing and
+/// line-wrapping differences between CLI versions.
+fn condense(text: &str) -> String {
+    text.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace()).collect()
+}
+
+fn first_line(text: &str) -> String {
+    text.lines()
+        .map(str::trim)
+        .find(|line| !line.is_empty())
+        .unwrap_or("no output")
+        .to_string()
+}
+
+#[cfg(test)]
+mod tests {
+    use super::*;
+
+    fn probe() -> AuthProbe {
+        AuthProbe {
+            args: vec!["auth".to_string(), "status".to_string()],
+            logged_in_substring: Some("\"loggedIn\": true".to_string()),
+            logged_out_substring: Some("\"loggedIn\": false".to_string()),
+            login_try_lines: vec!["claude login".to_string()],
+            timeout_seconds: Some(2),
+        }
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn logged_in_marker_matches_across_whitespace_variants() {
+        for raw in [
+            "{\n  \"loggedIn\": true,\n  \"authMethod\": \"claude.ai\"\n}",
+            "{\"loggedIn\":true}",
+        ] {
+            assert_eq!(classify_probe_output(&probe(), raw), CliAuthStatus::LoggedIn);
+        }
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn logged_out_marker_wins_over_embedded_logged_in_phrase() {
+        let codex_probe = AuthProbe {
+            args: vec!["login".to_string(), "status".to_string()],
+            logged_in_substring: Some("Logged in".to_string()),
+            logged_out_substring: Some("Not logged in".to_string()),
+            login_try_lines: vec!["codex login".to_string()],
+            timeout_seconds: Some(2),
+        };
+        assert!(matches!(
+            classify_probe_output(&codex_probe, "Not logged in"),
+            CliAuthStatus::NotLoggedIn { .. }
+        ));
+        assert_eq!(
+            classify_probe_output(&codex_probe, "Logged in using ChatGPT"),
+            CliAuthStatus::LoggedIn
+        );
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn unmatched_output_is_unknown_not_logged_out() {
+        assert!(matches!(
+            classify_probe_output(&probe(), "fake provider says hi"),
+            CliAuthStatus::Unknown { .. }
+        ));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn missing_binary_is_unknown() {
+        let status = probe_cli_auth("/nonexistent/deadreckon-test-binary", &probe());
+        assert!(matches!(status, CliAuthStatus::Unknown { .. }));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn real_subprocess_logged_out_classifies() {
+        let temp = tempfile::TempDir::new().expect("tempdir");
+        let script = temp.path().join("fake-cli");
+        std::fs::write(&script, "#!/bin/sh\necho '{\"loggedIn\": false}'\nexit 1\n")
+            .expect("write script");
+        #[cfg(unix)]
+        {
+            use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
+            std::fs::set_permissions(&script, std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o755))
+                .expect("chmod");
+        }
+        let status = probe_cli_auth(&script.display().to_string(), &probe());
+        assert!(matches!(status, CliAuthStatus::NotLoggedIn { .. }));
+    }
+}

+/// The binary a CLI route will actually execute: config override first, then
+/// the descriptor default.
+fn cli_binary_for(
+    config_path: &Path,
+    provider: Option<&str>,
+    descriptor: &ProviderDescriptor,
+) -> Option<String> {
+    let configured = provider.and_then(|provider| {
+        read_config(config_path)
+            .ok()?
+            .providers
+            .get(provider)
+            .and_then(|entry| entry.binary.clone())
+    });
+    configured.or_else(|| descriptor.default_binary.clone())
+}

103	        };
104	    }
105	    if let Some(in_marker) = probe.logged_in_substring.as_deref()
106	        && condensed.contains(&condense(in_marker))
107	    {
108	        return CliAuthStatus::LoggedIn;
109	    }
110	    CliAuthStatus::Unknown {
111	        reason: "auth probe output did not match a known login state".to_string(),
112	    }
113	}
114	
115	/// Strip all whitespace so marker matching survives JSON pretty-printing and
116	/// line-wrapping differences between CLI versions.
117	fn condense(text: &str) -> String {
118	    text.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace()).collect()
119	}
120	
121	fn first_line(text: &str) -> String {
122	    text.lines()
123	        .map(str::trim)
124	        .find(|line| !line.is_empty())
125	        .unwrap_or("no output")
126	        .to_string()
127	}

168	pub(crate) fn auto_subscription_cli_provider(registry: &ProviderRegistry) -> Option<String> {
169	    let providers = registry
170	        .iter()
171	        .filter(|descriptor| {
172	            descriptor.kind == DescriptorKind::Cli
173	                && descriptor.subscription
174	                && descriptor
175	                    .default_binary
176	                    .as_deref()
177	                    .is_some_and(crate::command_exists)
178	        })
179	        .map(|descriptor| descriptor.id.clone())
180	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
181	    if providers.len() == 1 {
182	        providers.into_iter().next()
183	    } else {
184	        None
185	    }
186	}

188	pub(crate) fn select_provider_setup(
189	    config_path: &Path,
190	    registry: &ProviderRegistry,
191	    request: ProviderSetupRequest<'_>,
192	) -> Result<ProviderSetupSelection, SetupRefusal> {
193	    let role = request.role.owned();
194	    let (provider, source) = provider_candidate(&request);
195	    let Some(provider) = provider else {
196	        if request.use_router_default {
197	            return selection_for_route(
198	                config_path,
199	                registry,
200	                role,
201	                None,
202	                request.explicit_model,
203	                SetupProviderSource::BuiltInDefault,
204	                request.require_usable_route,
205	            );
206	        }
207	        let mut selection = ProviderSetupSelection::none(role);
208	        selection
209	            .try_lines
210	            .push("deadreckon config provider cli:codex".to_string());
211	        return Ok(selection);
212	    };
213	    let provider = provider.trim();
214	    if provider.is_empty() {
215	        let mut selection = ProviderSetupSelection::none(role);
216	        selection
217	            .try_lines
218	            .push("deadreckon config provider cli:codex".to_string());
219	        return Ok(selection);
220	    }
221	    if !provider_route_exists(config_path, registry, provider) {
222	        return Err(SetupRefusal::unknown_provider(provider));
223	    }
224	
225	    selection_for_route(
226	        config_path,
227	        registry,
228	        role,
229	        Some(provider),
230	        request.explicit_model,
231	        source,
232	        request.require_usable_route,
233	    )
234	}
235	
236	fn selection_for_route(
237	    config_path: &Path,
238	    registry: &ProviderRegistry,
239	    role: SetupProviderRole,
240	    provider: Option<&str>,
241	    model: Option<&str>,
242	    source: SetupProviderSource,
243	    require_usable_route: bool,
244	) -> Result<ProviderSetupSelection, SetupRefusal> {
245	    let route = route_info_for_provider(config_path, provider, model)
246	        .map_err(|err| setup_refusal_for_provider_error(provider, err))?;
247	    let descriptor = provider
248	        .and_then(|provider| registry.get(provider))
249	        .or_else(|| {
250	            route
251	                .as_ref()
252	                .and_then(|route| registry.get(route.name.as_str()))
253	        });
254	    let mut selection = ProviderSetupSelection {
255	        role,
256	        provider: Some(
257	            route
258	                .as_ref()
259	                .map(|route| route.name.clone())
260	                .or_else(|| provider.map(ToString::to_string))
261	                .unwrap_or_default(),
262	        ),
263	        model: route
264	            .as_ref()
265	            .map(|route| route.model.clone())
266	            .or_else(|| model.map(ToString::to_string)),
267	        source,
268	        kind: descriptor
269	            .map(|descriptor| descriptor_kind_label(&descriptor.kind).to_string())
270	            .or_else(|| route.as_ref().map(|route| provider_kind_label(&route.kind))),
271	        credential: Some(provider_credential_label(descriptor, route.as_ref())),
272	        install_hint: descriptor.and_then(first_install_hint),
273	        warnings: Vec::new(),
274	        try_lines: Vec::new(),
275	    };
276	    if route.as_ref().is_some_and(|route| !route.has_credential) {
277	        if let Some(provider) = selection.provider.as_deref() {
278	            selection.warnings.push(format!(
279	                "provider {provider} needs credentials or an installed binary"
280	            ));
281	        }
282	        if let Some(hint) = selection.install_hint.clone() {
283	            selection.try_lines.push(hint);
284	        } else if let Some(provider) = selection.provider.as_deref() {
285	            selection.try_lines.push(format!(
286	                "deadreckon config set providers.{provider}.api_key <KEY>"
287	            ));
288	        }
289	        if require_usable_route {
290	            let provider_label = selection
291	                .provider
292	                .as_deref()
293	                .or(provider)
294	                .unwrap_or("provider");
295	            return Err(SetupRefusal {
296	                message: selection
297	                    .warnings
298	                    .first()
299	                    .cloned()
300	                    .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("provider {provider_label} is not usable")),
301	                try_line: selection
302	                    .try_lines
303	                    .first()
304	                    .cloned()
305	                    .unwrap_or_else(|| "deadreckon providers list --all".to_string()),
306	            });
307	        }
308	    }
309	    // An installed subscription CLI is not necessarily a usable one: probe
310	    // login state on the launch path (not previews) and refuse up front with
311	    // the provider's own login command instead of failing mid-run with raw
312	    // subprocess stderr. Unknown probe results fall through unchanged.
313	    if require_usable_route
314	        && route.as_ref().is_some_and(|route| route.has_credential)
315	        && let Some(descriptor) = descriptor
316	        && descriptor.kind == DescriptorKind::Cli
317	        && let Some(probe) = descriptor.auth_probe.as_ref()
318	        && let Some(binary) = cli_binary_for(config_path, selection.provider.as_deref(), descriptor)
319	        && let CliAuthStatus::NotLoggedIn { detail } = probe_cli_auth(&binary, probe)
320	    {
321	        let provider_label = selection.provider.as_deref().or(provider).unwrap_or("provider");
322	        return Err(SetupRefusal {
323	            message: format!("provider {provider_label} is installed but not logged in ({detail})"),
324	            try_line: probe
325	                .login_try_lines
326	                .first()
327	                .cloned()
328	                .unwrap_or_else(|| "deadreckon doctor".to_string()),
329	        });
330	    }
331	    Ok(selection)
332	}

334	/// The binary a CLI route will actually execute: config override first, then
335	/// the descriptor default.
336	fn cli_binary_for(
337	    config_path: &Path,
338	    provider: Option<&str>,
339	    descriptor: &ProviderDescriptor,
340	) -> Option<String> {
341	    let configured = provider.and_then(|provider| {
342	        read_config(config_path)
343	            .ok()?
344	            .providers
345	            .get(provider)
346	            .and_then(|entry| entry.binary.clone())
347	    });
348	    configured.or_else(|| descriptor.default_binary.clone())
349	}

351	fn provider_candidate<'a>(
352	    request: &ProviderSetupRequest<'a>,
353	) -> (Option<&'a str>, SetupProviderSource) {
354	    if let Some(provider) = non_empty(request.explicit_provider) {
355	        return (Some(provider), SetupProviderSource::Flag);
356	    }
357	    if matches!(request.role, SetupProviderRoleRef::DocPolish)
358	        && let Some(provider) = non_empty(request.config_doc_provider)
359	    {
360	        return (Some(provider), SetupProviderSource::Config);
361	    }
362	    if !matches!(request.role, SetupProviderRoleRef::DocPolish)
363	        && let Some(provider) = non_empty(request.config_default_provider)
364	    {
365	        return (Some(provider), SetupProviderSource::Config);
366	    }
367	    if request.allow_auto_subscription
368	        && let Some(provider) = non_empty(request.auto_subscription_provider)
369	    {
370	        return (Some(provider), SetupProviderSource::AutoSubscription);
371	    }
372	    if let Some(provider) = non_empty(request.run_provider) {
373	        return (Some(provider), SetupProviderSource::RunProvider);
374	    }
375	    if let Some(provider) = non_empty(request.built_in_default_provider) {
376	        return (Some(provider), SetupProviderSource::BuiltInDefault);
377	    }
378	    (None, SetupProviderSource::None)
379	}

419	fn provider_credential_label(
420	    descriptor: Option<&ProviderDescriptor>,
421	    route: Option<&ProviderRouteInfo>,
422	) -> String {
423	    let has_credential = route.is_some_and(|route| route.has_credential);
424	    match descriptor {
425	        Some(descriptor) if descriptor.subscription && has_credential => "subscription",
426	        Some(descriptor) if descriptor.subscription => "missing",
427	        Some(descriptor) if descriptor.auth.kind == AuthKind::None && has_credential => "none",
428	        Some(_) if has_credential => "ready",
429	        Some(_) => "missing",
430	        None if has_credential => "ready",
431	        None => "missing",
432	    }
433	    .to_string()
434	}

544	            None => self.source.as_str().to_string(),
545	        }
546	    }
547	
548	    fn with_path(
549	        source: DoneCriteriaSource,
550	        path: PathBuf,
551	        companion_doc: Option<PathBuf>,
552	        checks: Option<usize>,
553	    ) -> Self {
554	        let label = match checks {
555	            Some(checks) => format!("{} ({checks} checks)", source.as_str()),
556	            None => source.as_str().to_string(),
557	        };
558	        Self {
559	            source,
560	            path: Some(path),
561	            companion_doc,
562	            checks,
563	            label,
564	            technical_label: ".deadreckon/acceptance.yaml".to_string(),
565	            try_lines: vec!["deadreckon def-done \"what should count as done\"".to_string()],
566	        }
567	    }
568	}

325	        let mut registry = Self::builtin()?;

327	        let mut paths = match fs::read_dir(&overrides_dir) {
328	            Ok(entries) => entries
329	                .filter_map(std::result::Result::ok)
330	                .map(|entry| entry.path())
331	                .filter(|path| path.extension().and_then(|ext| ext.to_str()) == Some("toml"))
332	                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
333	            Err(source) if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(registry),
334	            Err(source) => {
335	                return Err(ProviderError::Io {
336	                    path: overrides_dir.display().to_string(),

341	        paths.sort();

343	            registry.load_override(&path)?;

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-06-09 18:25:52Z)**_

After reading all changed files and tracing the new sink (subprocess `Command::new(binary).args(probe.args)`), I conclude there's no new vulnerability worth flagging:

1. **Subprocess sink (`probe_cli_auth`)** — `binary` is the same path the user has already configured for execution by deadreckon; `probe.args` come from baked-in TOML descriptors (`auth status`, `login status`). `Command::new` does not go through a shell, so injection isn't possible, and the binary was going to be executed by deadreckon anyway (e.g., version probe in doctor.rs, exec_template at run time). No new attack surface.

2. **Classification logic** — `classify_probe_output` checks `logged_out_substring` FIRST (correctly handles the "Not logged in" / "Logged in" substring overlap), and unknown output collapses to `Unknown` which preserves prior presence-only behavior. Both shipped descriptors define both markers, so the embedded-phrase footgun doesn't bite. Fail-open here is the documented and correct posture — Unknown reduces to old behavior.

3. **`first_line(combined)` detail leak** — surfaced in `SetupRefusal.message` and `DoctorFinding.detail`, which display the user's own auth-probe output back to that same user on their own machine. Not a sensitive-to-observability finding (no cross-principal log/trace/metric sink; no upstream attacker-controlled secret).

4. **Process management** — timeout path kills + waits; OS pipe buffers limit unbounded growth, and even the worst case is volumetric (out of scope).

5. **Sibling-path gate parity** — the new probe is gated only on the launch path (`require_usable_route`), as designed; preview path intentionally skips it, which matches the comment and is tested.

6. **`cli_binary_for`** — reads the same config the rest of the launch path reads; binary value is user's own.

7. **Registry override (`providers.d/*.toml`)** — could supply custom `auth_probe.args` and `login_try_lines`, but the user owns `~/.deadreckon/`; the same user could already supply `exec_template`. No new privilege boundary crossed.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-06-09 18:26:00Z)**_

No security findings. The auth probe spawns the user-configured binary with descriptor-static args (`auth status` / `login status`) — same binary deadreckon would execute anyway — using `Command::new` (no shell), with timeout, kill, and fail-open `Unknown` classification that preserves prior presence-only behavior. The `detail` substring shown to users in refusal/finding messages comes from the user's own CLI on their own machine (not a cross-principal observability sink). Classification correctly checks `logged_out_substring` before `logged_in_substring` to avoid the "Not logged in" ⊃ "Logged in" substring overlap, and both shipped descriptors define both markers.
